records.text: Paper card. Question: How does the multication composition in high-entropy perovskite oxides contribute to high catalytic activity for the oxygen evolution reaction?. System: High-entropy perovskite oxides (HEO), specifically LaCr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2O3-δ. Processing: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD) with a laser fluence of 1.8 J/cm2 and a frequency of 10 Hz at an oxygen pressure of 0.04 mbar. Test conditions: O2-saturated 0.1 M potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution, three-electrode configuration, rotation disk electrode (RDE) setup. Findings: 15.47; 680.0; 51.0; 128.0; 45.0. Mechanism: Synergistic effect of simultaneous oxidation and reduction of different transition metal cations during the adsorption of reaction intermediates. Limitations: The exact reaction mechanism for high-entropy oxides is not yet identified and needs further investigation. Future work: Detailed future clarification of the OER on P-HEO materials and possible synergistic roles of multiple active sites to enable further electrocatalyst optimization. Quote: "the activity of P-HEO remains higher than that for the parent compounds"
